chapters.title: Introduction
chapters.html:
In Quebec, no sale of real estate is concluded without a notary. This legal professional secures the transaction, protects the parties and makes the sale official. Knowing it means approaching the signature with peace of mind.

This guide explains the role of the notary, the signing process, and the costs associated with it.

Informative content. Each chapter ends with a lined “My Notes” page.

In Quebec, no sale of real estate is concluded without a notary. This legal professional secures the transaction, protects the parties and makes the sale official. This guide explains its role, what it checks, how the signing takes place and the associated costs.

Knowing it means approaching the signature with peace of mind.

chapters.title: An impartial public officer
chapters.html:
Understand your particular position.

The notary is a public officer : he acts impartially to give the deed of sale its official force. He verifies, writes, authenticates and preserves the documents.

Its role is to secure the transaction for all the parties, not to defend just one. In a purchase, it is usually the buyer who chooses the notary - often because it is he (or his lender) who assumes the costs.

  • Impartiality: he does not take sides.
  • Authentic force: the act he receives is proof.
  • Conservation: it keeps the original (the minute).

The notary is not “your lawyer”: he acts impartially to give the sale its official force and secure all parties. In a purchase, it is usually the buyer who chooses it, often because he assumes the costs.

Emilie's advice

The notary is not “your lawyer”. It protects the validity of the sale for everyone. If there is an issue between you and the seller, you need your own advisor, not the notary.

chapters.title: What the notary checks and prepares
chapters.objective: Know the work behind the signature.
chapters.html:
Know the work behind the signature.

Most of the work of the notary is done before on the day of signing:

  • Title review : confirm that the seller is the owner, without hidden charges (mortgage, seizure).
  • Analysis of certificate of location and easements.
  • Writing of theact of sale and the mortgage deed.
  • Receipt and redistribution of funds (repayment of the old mortgage, payment to the seller).
  • Publication of the sale in the Land Register.

It is this meticulous work that saves you from unpleasant surprises after the purchase.

Most of his work is done before signing: examination of the titles (is the seller the owner, without hidden charges?), analysis of the certificate of location and easements, drafting of the deeds, then receipt and redistribution of funds. This meticulous work prevents you from unpleasant surprises after the purchase.

Emilie's advice

Provide your documents to the notary as soon as possible. A complete file sent on time means a stress-free signature and sometimes a few days saved.

chapters.title: Signature and fees
chapters.objective: Know what to expect on the big day.
chapters.html:
Know what to expect on the big day.

On the day of signing, the notary explains the deed to you, answers your questions, collects the signatures and makes the payments. This is also when you receive the keys (according to the agreed possession date).

On the budget side, include in your closing costs:

  • The fees of the notary.
  • The disbursements : publication costs, copies, research.

Useful reminder: the welcome tax is not paid at the notary - it is the subject of a municipal invoice sent a few weeks or months later.

On the big day, the notary explains the deed, collects the signatures and makes the payments. Include fees and disbursements (publication, copies) in your closing costs. Reminder: the welcome tax is not paid at the notary, but by municipal invoice later.

Emilie's advice

Ask the notary for a written estimate of costs from the outset. You will avoid the surprise of “how much I have to bring” the day before signing.

chapters.title: Choose and prepare your notary well
chapters.objective: Approach signing with peace of mind.
chapters.html:
Approach the signature with peace of mind.

The choice of notary is often left to the buyer. Some guidelines to help you decide:

  • A recommendation from your broker or lender is a good place to start.
  • Check its availability in relation to your closing date.
  • Make sure it answers your questions clearly.

Prepare for your part: valid identity documents, bank details, proof of home insurance in force for the date of possession. Having a ready file speeds everything up.

Contact the notary as soon as the promise is accepted, not the day before: good notaries are busy and a signature is being planned. Have your identification documents, bank details and proof of current insurance ready - a complete file speeds everything up.

Emilie's advice

Contact the notary as soon as the promise to purchase is accepted, not the week before. Good notaries are busy, and a signing must be planned several weeks in advance.

chapters.title: After signing: what remains
chapters.objective: Understand the consequences of the sale.
chapters.html:
Understand the consequences of the sale.

The signing isn't quite the end. The notary completes a few more steps:

  • Publication Official of the sale and mortgage in the Land Register.
  • Disbarment of the seller's old mortgage.
  • Sending copies of the act to the parties.

For your part, keep your copy of the deed of sale carefully: it will be used for your taxes, a future resale, or any questions about the property.

After signing, the notary publishes the sale in the Land Register, cancels the old mortgage and sends the copies. Keep your bill of sale carefully: it will be used for your taxes, a future resale or any questions about the property.

Emilie's advice

Store your bill of sale and your certificate of location in a safe place. The day you resell, these documents will save you valuable time.

chapters.title: Action plan
chapters.html:
Your next steps, concretely.

This week

  1. Choose a notary (often recommended by the broker or lender).
  2. Gather my documents and ID.

Within 30 days

  1. Have titles and certificate of location examined.
  2. Budget fees and disbursements.

Then

  1. Sign having understood the act, questions asked.

For a peaceful signature

  1. Choose and contact the notary as soon as the promise is accepted.
  2. Prepare my documents, funds and proof of insurance in advance.
